bullets.title: NVDA Rubin Ultra may cut HBM content amid advanced memory shortage
bullets.body: Multiple sources report NVIDIA is considering reducing high-bandwidth memory in its Rubin Ultra GPU design to address a shortage of advanced HBM chips. The Information cited the potential design change; one fintwit account noted this is 'not good for memory' suppliers, implying negative read-through for HBM incumbents.

bullets.title: Semiconductor test cycle inflecting: Advantest TAM up sharply, OSATS at record capex
bullets.body: Advantest raised its 2026 memory test TAM to $2.75B (+12%) and SoC TAM to $11B (+21%). ASE tester deployment is running at 2x prior peak and Q2 OSAT test capex hit an all-time high (~2x prior high). Teradyne confirmed test equipment is now outgrowing fab equipment for the first time in a decade, with memory book-to-bill >2, pointing to a second demand leg beyond SoC.

bullets.title: InP shortage worsening; Lumentum CEO calls it more severe than DRAM/NAND; AXTI in focus
bullets.body: Lumentum's CEO flagged a 'severe and worsening' indium phosphide shortage that now exceeds constraints in DRAM and NAND markets. AXTI recently signed a partnership with LITE, and one analyst noted the NOK InP supply issue points to a manufacturing/testing bottleneck rather than broad optics shortage—implying AXTI's situation is idiosyncratic, not sector-wide.

bullets.title: GOOGL raises $25B in bonds; draws $115B demand—hyperscaler spreads blow out
bullets.body: Alphabet is raising up to $25B across as many as 10 tranches (2–40 year maturities) to fund AI capex, drawing roughly $115B in investor demand. One account noted GOOGL has raised $30B+ in February, $25B in November, and now again, effectively funding capex entirely with debt. Investment-grade spreads are expected to widen across hyperscaler names.

bullets.title: Tesla's Terafab: 1+ TW of compute/year target; Musk estimates 25% for Optimus, 75% AI/spacecraft
bullets.body: Tesla confirmed Terafab will be built in Grimes County, Texas, targeting over 1 terawatt of annual compute output. Musk's 'very approximate guess' allocates ~25% to Tesla Optimus and ~75% to AI/spacecraft applications; Terafab is also hiring memory process engineers, signaling a serious push into DRAM manufacturing that analysts say threatens the Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron oligopoly.

bullets.title: MTSI blowout guide: Q4 EPS $1.97–$2.03 vs. $1.48 consensus
bullets.body: MACOM Technology guided Q4 adjusted EPS to $1.97–$2.03 versus the $1.48 consensus estimate, with revenue of $415–$425M, a substantial beat that reflects continued strength in its RF/optical product lines.

bullets.title: AAOI pre-earnings: Q3 guide is the key—below $270M would be 'concerning'
bullets.body: One analyst framing AAOI Q2 as a 'bridge quarter' at ~$190M revenue and 29.5% gross margin. The real inflection is Q3: a guide below $270M would be concerning for the $1.1B annual revenue target, while $300–$320M would be needed to stay on track. The stock is positioned as a Q3 guide story.

bullets.title: VIAV solid quarter: data center revenue doubles YoY, now 40% of sales
bullets.body: Viasat reported beats across revenue, margins, and EPS. Data center now represents roughly 40% of total company revenue and more than doubled year-over-year on an organic basis (excluding Spirent), signaling meaningful exposure to AI infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: CIEN's WaveLogic 6 Extreme can encrypt 1.6 Tb/s using QKD keys at wire speed
bullets.body: Fintwit semiconductor analyst clarified that Ciena's WaveLogic 6 Extreme platform can integrate QKD-generated keys to encrypt 1.6 Tb/s of conventional traffic at wire speed—the 1.6T figure refers to conventional encrypted data, not quantum throughput, an important distinction for the quantum networking investment thesis.

bullets.title: Memory stocks ($MU, $SNDK): supercycle thesis questioned after 6-month run
bullets.body: One fintwit account asked whether the memory supercycle trade is 'starting to unwind' after MU and SNDK minted fortunes in 6 months. Jefferies cut its SNDK price target 42% from $3,000 to $1,750 while maintaining Buy. South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.6%, with SK Hynix -10.4% and Samsung -6.3%, reflecting broader memory sector stress.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran drafts bill to ban US/Israeli vessels; US says routes unimpeded
bullets.body: Iran's parliament is reviewing a preliminary bill that would ban U.S., Israeli, and 'hostile' vessels from the Strait of Hormuz, with fines up to 20% of cargo value for violations. U.S. officials counter that no single party controls the strait and temporary routes will operate without impediment. Brent crude jumped above $82/bbl intraday on the headlines.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike probability rises to ~70%; BofA now expects three hikes this year
bullets.body: Prediction markets show ~70% probability of a Fed rate hike this year, with Bank of America revising its call to three hikes. Fed Chair Warsh is reportedly prepared to support a September hike per FT, though colleagues leaking guidance to media undercuts his stated goal of eliminating forward guidance. Yardeni argues the Fed should turn more hawkish given consumer spending +3.3% and business investment +8.4%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 call volume hits record 4M contracts; Tom Lee targets 7,900–8,000 in August
bullets.body: S&P 500 call option volume exceeded 4 million contracts Tuesday for the first time ever, driven by FOMO and improving earnings breadth. Fundstrat's Tom Lee expects the index to reach 7,900–8,000 this month (3.6% upside from Wednesday's close); Kalshi traders assign 66.9% probability of hitting 8,000 in 2026. A $2.7B call wall sits at SPY 775.

bullets.title: US macro data strong: jobless claims 199K (est. 205K), productivity +1.4% (est. 0.6%)
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 199K for the week of August 1, well below the 205K consensus, nearing 57-year lows. Q2 labor productivity beat sharply at +1.4% QoQ versus +0.6% expected, while unit labor costs rose only 1.3% versus 2.1% forecast—a combination that supports the soft-landing narrative and gives the Fed ammunition to hike.

bullets.title: MSFT: OpenAI accounts for ~70% of AI revenue; opens 4th India data center under $20.5B plan
bullets.body: OpenAI is reported to represent roughly 70% of Microsoft's AI revenue, highlighting concentration risk in the partnership. Separately, Microsoft opened its fourth AI data center region in India as part of a broader $20.5 billion investment in cloud and AI infrastructure. One account noted MSFT is the only major tech name currently showing positive free cash flow.

bullets.title: PLTR: contrarian view—shorting down 20% with improving fundamentals is poor risk/reward
bullets.body: One fintwit account argues that shorting Palantir after a 20% decline while fundamentals are improving represents bad risk/reward. They note PLTR was previously a 'peak-fundies crowded long' but the current setup favors the long side post-selloff.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex on track to reach 3% of GDP by 2027–2029; token prices moderating enterprise AI diffusion
bullets.body: One analyst notes consensus now expects hyperscaler capex to become a permanent feature of the economy, rising from 0.3% of GDP in 2019 and 1.4% in 2025 to ~3% by 2027–2029. A separate analyst argues current token prices are acting as a brake on enterprise AI adoption—if prices fell, compute demand would be 'significantly higher.'

bullets.title: Nvidia seeking Chinese suppliers for 6G AI-RAN base stations; also igniting RF market
bullets.body: Nvidia is 'urgently' seeking AI base station suppliers in China to develop 6G AI-RAN equipment, which handles both communication and AI computing tasks. A semiconductor analyst separately noted that 'Nvidia will ignite the RF market,' suggesting meaningful downstream opportunity for RF component names.

bullets.title: AI semiconductor drawdown context: July 2026 was worst month since 2002, $1T in market value lost
bullets.body: One analyst characterized July 2026 as the 'sharpest drawdown of the AI cycle' with semiconductors posting their worst monthly performance since 2002 and more than $1 trillion in AI-linked market value erased. The analyst identifies compute as the 'deepest moat' in LLM competition.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: California AG time-run strategy; June 4, 2027 is the critical merger deadline
bullets.body: LightShed analyst notes California AG Rob Bonta is running a clock-based litigation strategy rather than seeking outright victory—and it 'appears to be succeeding.' The critical date for the Paramount/WBD merger outcome is June 4, 2027; Paramount could win legally but still lose the deal entirely.
